input.question: how do we sense touch?
input.ground_truth: Well its important you understand that you cannot ever actually touch anything. You can get very, very close to touching it. For all meaningful purposes it appears you are touching it, but you are not. On the smallest scales, the atoms that make up your body repel the atoms making up everything else. So when you feel touch, you are feeling electromagnetic forces acting against you. The specific patterns of it trigger specific nerve impulses. (which is itself electrical) The way the atoms are organized in one object or texture is different from how they are organized in another object or texture. These very small differences are readily picked up by your nervous system because it works on equally small scales. It gets used to associating certain electromagnetic reactions with certain things.
